evals.prompt: Check Amazon Keyspaces CQL compatibility for our Apache Cassandra 3.11 schema that uses: (1) a `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`, (2) a `CREATE CUSTOM INDEX` (SASI), (3) a Lua User-Defined Function (`CREATE FUNCTION`), (4) an `UNLOGGED BATCH` containing an `INSERT ... IF NOT EXISTS` LWT, and (5) a User-Defined Type (`CREATE TYPE address`) with static columns and row-level `USING TTL`.
evals.expected_output: Follows **Mode 3 (`mode-3-compatibility`)** (`references/mode-3-compatibility.md`): announces `references/mode-3-compatibility.md`, prints the `check-compatibility.ts` command, and accurately classifies **(1) Materialized Views = UNSUPPORTED** (use dual-write/CDC + denormalized query table), **(2) SASI / secondary indexes = UNSUPPORTED** (model dedicated query tables), **(3) UDFs/UDAs = UNSUPPORTED** (move logic to app/Lambda), **(4) LWT (`IF NOT EXISTS` / `IF`) inside `UNLOGGED BATCH` = UNSUPPORTED** (Keyspaces rejects conditional statements inside `UNLOGGED BATCH` — execute standalone single-partition LWT or regular logged/conditional patterns per docs), and **(5) UDTs (`CREATE TYPE`), static columns, and `USING TTL` = SUPPORTED**.
expectations: Activates the amazon-keyspaces skill and references `mode-3-compatibility` (`references/mode-3-compatibility.md`)
Flags Materialized Views, SASI/secondary indexes, UDFs, and LWT (`IF NOT EXISTS`) inside `UNLOGGED BATCH` as UNSUPPORTED with Keyspaces remediation patterns
Confirms UDTs (`CREATE TYPE`), static columns, and `USING TTL` are SUPPORTED in Amazon Keyspaces

evals.prompt: Our Java DataStax 4.x driver connecting to `cassandra.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com:9042` with `ConsistencyLevel.ONE` on writes fails with connection timeouts and `InvalidQueryException` consistency errors. Fix both issues.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses every Keyspaces connectivity mismatch (`references/keyspaces-modes-and-troubleshooting.md`): (1) **Amazon Keyspaces listens on TLS port `9142` (NOT default Cassandra plaintext `9042`)** and requires TLS (`Amazon Root CA` / Starfield truststore) plus VPC endpoint `com.amazonaws.ap-south-1.cassandra` or NAT egress; (2) authenticate with the **AWS SigV4 auth plugin** (`software.aws.mcs.auth.SigV4AuthProvider`, IAM role credentials — never static hardcoded keys); and (3) **writes in Keyspaces ONLY support `LOCAL_QUORUM`** (`ONE`, `QUORUM`, `ALL` fail with `InvalidQueryException`; reads support `LOCAL_ONE`, `ONE`, or `LOCAL_QUORUM`).
expectations: Activates the amazon-keyspaces skill
Fixes port `9042 -> 9142` with mandatory TLS CA truststore and AWS `SigV4AuthProvider` authentication
Fixes write consistency from `ConsistencyLevel.ONE` to `LOCAL_QUORUM` (explaining Keyspaces rejects `ONE` on writes)

expectations: Activates the amazon-keyspaces skill
Confirms switching a table between `AWS_OWNED_KMS_KEY` and `CUSTOMER_MANAGED_KMS_KEY` executes online with zero downtime
Warns clearly that adding a Region via `update-keyspace --replication-specification` is irreversible (regions cannot be removed once added) and recommends testing on a separate keyspace first

evals.prompt: Verify via AWS documentation MCP tools how **Amazon Keyspaces Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)** restores work (`restore-table` target behavior and retention window) and how **Time to Live (TTL)** expiration deletes are metered compared to regular `DELETE` statements.
evals.expected_output: Consults `awsknowledge` / `aws-mcp` documentation tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands and confirms: (1) **Keyspaces PITR** provides continuous per-second backups over a **35-day rolling window**, and `restore-table` **always creates a brand-new table** (never overwrites the live source table in place; takes minutes to hours depending on size, after which applications cut over); and (2) **Keyspaces TTL** (`default_time_to_live` / CQL `USING TTL`) expires rows automatically within ~10 days of expiry at a dedicated **discounted TTL delete per-KB rate** without consuming provisioned/on-demand table write capacity (unlike explicit CQL `DELETE` statements which consume full WRUs/WCUs).
expectations: Activates the amazon-keyspaces skill and consults `awsknowledge` / `aws-mcp` documentation tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands
Confirms Keyspaces PITR covers a 35-day continuous window and `restore-table` always restores into a new target table without overwriting the source table
Contrasts TTL automatic expiration billing (separate discounted TTL delete pricing without consuming table write capacity) against explicit CQL `DELETE` WRU/WCU consumption
